text: I've had this cough going on for about eight weeks now, and it started dry but has since become productive with clear sputum. speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient
text: The sputum is clear and watery, and I do notice some mild wheezing when I breathe hard. Yes, I have been diagnosed with high blood pressure, though I don't have a history of heart disease. speaker: Doctor
text: Understood, I will proceed with a clinical evaluation only. When you exert yourself, does the wheezing occur at the beginning of your breath or at the end of your exhale? Additionally, does taking a deep breath into cold air trigger the cough or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: The wheezing tends to happen mostly at the end of my exhale when I'm trying to catch my breath. Taking a deep breath in cold air does seem to make the coughing and tightness in my chest a bit worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Asthma (likely exacerbated by cold air and exertion). Given the 8-week duration of cough with clear sputum, exertional dyspnea, wheezing at the end of expiration, and worsening with cold air, this clinical picture strongly points to an asthma exacerbation or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) given your hypertension, but the clear sputum and cold air trigger favor asthma. Since labs are restricted, I recommend a trial of inhaled bronchodilators and monitoring for relief.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Acute exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
